digest.top_line: DBCG IMN2: IMNI in node-positive breast cancer → adjusted OS HR 0.85 (0.76-0.94), 15y OS 65.0% vs 60.8%; cohort allocated by laterality, not randomized.
digest.tldr: Elective nodal RT led in breast and prostate. DBCG IMN2, a nonrandomized population-based cohort, links IMNI in node-positive breast cancer to an adjusted OS HR of 0.85. PEACE V-STORM, a phase 2 RCT (α 0.20), favours whole-pelvis ENRT over MDT for pelvic nodal oligorecurrence (4yr MFS 76% vs 63%, HR 0.62). EORTC endorses reduced-dose RT for cutaneous lymphoma without randomized evidence.

sites.intro: EORTC expert opinion recommends reduced-dose RT across indolent cutaneous lymphomas, but registry data conflict on 4 Gy in pcMZL/pcFCL.

studies.name: EORTC cutaneous lymphoma RT recommendations
studies.tldr: Reduced-dose RT recommended across indolent cutaneous lymphomas; local MF lesions 8-12 Gy in 2-3 fx, 1-yr local control ≥92%, no randomized evidence.

details.text: 🔍 EORTC cutaneous lymphoma tumour group expert opinion (EJC 2024); dose algorithm to standardize RT across EORTC centres

details: ⚠️ Authors state no randomized trials support RT selection over other modalities

details.text: 🔗 Conventional 30-40 Gy was SOC until ~20 yrs ago; current regimens across Europe highly heterogeneous

subdetails: 4 Gy (1-2 fx) gave inferior local control
Low-dose 8-12 Gy to palliate skin disease in advanced MF
Up to 24 Gy to induce remission before autologous SCT
SS: controversial, rarely durable; lowers circulating Sézary counts

details: 📊 pcALCL: few relapses at doses of 20 Gy; palliative 2×4 Gy for symptoms
📊 CD4+ small/medium T-cell LPD: 4 Gy in 2 fx, 100% remission, no local relapses

subdetails: pcFCL/pcMZL: 4 Gy curative in many cases
Lesions >5 cm treated with 4 Gy had worse outcomes
Response-adapted escalation to cumulative 24 Gy for residual disease or local failure after 4 Gy
DLBCL leg type: consolidative RT after systemic; 30 Gy post-systemic reported equivalent

details: ⚠️ Registry data conflict on 4 Gy in pcMZL/pcFCL: one long-f/u retrospective series found inferior response and more in-field relapse vs higher doses
⚠️ Tables 1-2 pool small retrospective series with heterogeneous doses; row-level values not reliably extractable here
studies.significance: The de-escalation is not uniform: 4 Gy is endorsed for CD4+ small/medium T-cell LPD and many pcFCL/pcMZL, but gave inferior MF local control and worse outcomes in B-cell lesions >5 cm. The algorithm handles this with response-adapted escalation to cumulative 24 Gy rather than upfront conventional dosing.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Expert opinion** from the EORTC cutaneous lymphoma tumour group, summarizing retrospective series and small prospective cohorts into a **dose algorithm** (Figs 2A/2B). No new patient data.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: MF local lesions **8-12 Gy in 2-3 fx**; low-dose TSEBT **8-12 Gy** for palliation, up to **24 Gy** before autologous SCT. CD4+ small/medium T-cell LPD **4 Gy in 2 fx**; pcFCL/pcMZL start at 4 Gy with escalation to cumulative **24 Gy** for residual disease or local failure.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Moves away from conventional **30-40 Gy**, the standard until about 20 years ago, and builds on prior EORTC consensus treatment-selection recommendations. The 4 Gy question in cutaneous B-cell disease remains contested between small series and a long-f/u registry analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents indolent primary cutaneous lymphomas (MF, pcALCL, CD4+ small/medium T-cell LPD, pcMZL, pcFCL) and palliative or pre-transplant TSEBT in advanced MF/SS. Does not represent aggressive rare CTCL subtypes (panniculitis-like, gamma/delta, CD8+ aggressive epidermotropic, NK/T-cell), where low-dose RT has a limited role.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Supporting series use varied endpoints (ORR, CR, local relapse, DOR, TTNT) and heterogeneous fractionation, so cross-series comparison is loose. **QoL data** after modern doses are sparse.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Low-dose local RT gives rapid symptom relief with low toxicity and few local relapses, but low-dose TSEBT relapses are common. Authors call for a **prospective randomized dose trial** with translational endpoints, and combined-modality work in advanced MF, SS and DLBCL leg type.

studies.interpretation:
The central argument of this document is that the historic dose ceiling for cutaneous lymphoma was set far above what these diseases need. For decades 30 to 40 Gy was treated as curative dosing, and the recommendation here is essentially to reserve that range for the minority of cases where lower doses demonstrably fail. The radiobiology section offers a mechanistic rationale, citing TREX1 upregulation above 12 to 18 Gy as a brake on RT-induced immune signalling, but that argument comes from preclinical and translational work and should not carry much weight in a dose decision on its own. The clinical case rests on retrospective response and local relapse data.

That evidence base is the main reason to hold the recommendations loosely rather than dismiss them. The series pooled in Tables 1 and 2 are small, mostly single-institution, and report different endpoints. Response rates near 100% in indolent histologies are expected almost regardless of dose, so ORR says little about the right dose. Local relapse and durability are the endpoints that could separate dose levels, and those need follow-up long enough to cover the late relapses typical of indolent B-cell disease. That is exactly where the data conflict: small series showed comparable in-field control between ultra-low and higher doses in pcFCL/pcMZL, while a larger registry analysis with longer follow-up found 4 Gy inferior. The authors do not settle the disagreement. They route around it with a response-adapted strategy, starting low and escalating to a cumulative 24 Gy for residual or recurrent disease. That is a reasonable pragmatic answer, but it assumes salvage after local failure is as effective as upfront higher dosing, and nothing in the source tests that.

The recommendations are most secure where the data are cleanest and stakes are lowest. CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder at 4 Gy in two fractions, and MF plaques at 8 to 12 Gy, both have consistent local control, and the MF signal includes an explicit finding that 4 Gy underperforms, which gives a floor as well as a ceiling. The size caveat in B-cell disease (worse outcomes with 4 Gy for lesions over 5 cm) is the most practically useful selection detail in the paper, since it identifies a group where starting low may just add a treatment course.

For TSEBT the document is candid that low-dose regimens relapse often, and the case for lower doses is repeatability and toxicity rather than durability. Sézary syndrome and DLBCL leg type are framed as combined-modality problems, and the ongoing mogamulizumab and brentuximab trials with low-dose TSEBT are where that question will be answered. The call for a randomized dose trial is the right one; until it exists, these are well-reasoned defaults, not settled doses.

The algorithm handles this with response-adapted escalation to cumulative 24 Gy rather than upfront conventional dosing.

sites.intro: Population-based OS data now back IMNI in node-positive disease, including 1-3 LN (post hoc HR 0.85).

studies.name: DBCG IMN2
studies.tldr: Adjusted OS HR 0.85 (0.76-0.94) with IMNI in node-positive breast cancer; 15y OS 65.0% vs 60.8% despite taxanes, trastuzumab, AIs and 3D RT.
details: 🔍 Prospective nationwide population-based cohort, 6 RT centres, N=4541, treated 2007-2014
⚠️ Not randomized: IMNI allocated by laterality (right-sided IMNI, left-sided no IMNI) under national guideline
🔍 Macrometastatic node-positive, all ALND; excluded neoadjuvant systemic therapy, bilateral BC, prior malignancy

details.text: 📊 Efficacy by endpoint, ITT by laterality (median f/u 13.7y OS, 13.2y DM)

details: 📐 15y OS risk difference 4.2% (95% CI 0.9-7.5)
⚠️ Crude DM HR 0.91 (0.81-1.02), p=0.11; DM signal depends on adjustment

IMN target ICS 1-4; 3D conformal wide tangents, free breathing
Axilla level II-III, interpectoral and level IV in all; level I if ≥6 LN+ or <10 removed

details: ⚠️ Dose separation diluted: median IMN CTV V90% 94.6% right vs 20.4% left; 10.1% of left-sided got IMNI
📊 15y death from ischemic/valvular heart disease 0.2% right vs 0.7% left; left-sided median MHD 2.3 Gy

verdict.audience: Node-positive early breast, upfront surgery + ALND, no neoadjuvant therapy

studies.significance: The benefit held in the 1-3 node group, HR 0.85 (0.73-0.97), the population where guidelines still hedge on IMNI. It was delivered with free-breathing 3D wide tangents at 50 Gy/25 Fx, and dilution (20.4% incidental coverage left-sided) biases toward the null, so modern gated or VMAT coverage likely does no worse.
studies.monday_clinic: In node-positive breast cancer after upfront surgery and ALND, including 1-3 positive nodes, this supports covering the IMN in the regional field; it does not extend to pts treated after neoadjuvant therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective nationwide population-based cohort across 6 Danish RT centres, **N=4541**, 2007-2014. **Not randomized**: IMNI allocated by tumour laterality per national guideline; ITT right vs left. Median follow-up **13.7y**.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Macrometastatic node-positive** breast cancer, all with ALND, mastectomy or BCS. Excluded **neoadjuvant systemic therapy**, bilateral BC, prior malignancy, recurrence before RT. Median age 59; 68.3% had 1-3 positive nodes.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: EC x3 then docetaxel x3 when chemo indicated; AI postmenopausal, tamoxifen premenopausal; trastuzumab concurrent for HER2+. 96.2% of chemo pts received taxanes.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **48 Gy/24 Fx** before Jan 2009, **50 Gy/25 Fx** after. IMN target **ICS 1-4** with 3D conformal wide tangents, free breathing, plus level II-III, interpectoral and level IV in all pts.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** OS. **Secondary:** breast cancer mortality and distant metastasis, with non-breast-cancer death as competing event.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: 15y death from ischemic or valvular heart disease **0.2% right vs 0.7% left**. 15y secondary lung cancer death 1.8% vs 2.2%. No smoking or baseline cardiac data.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: OS HR 0.85 sits with the **EBCTCG** regional RT RR 0.90 (0.84-0.96) and underpowered **KROG 08-06** HR 0.87 (0.57-1.31). Magnitude matches **DBCG IMN1**, which treated pts before taxanes and 3D planning.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents node-positive early breast cancer after upfront surgery and ALND on taxane, AI and trastuzumab era systemic therapy. Does not represent pts after neoadjuvant therapy, pCR, or those receiving adjuvant IO or ADCs.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Left-sided controls got **incidental IMN dose** (median CTV V90% 20.4%) and 10.1% received IMNI, compressing separation. 1-3 node analysis was **post hoc**; no correction for multiple testing across subgroups.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Newer systemic therapy **did not erase** the IMNI gain. The medial/central ≥4 node HR 0.98 and ER-/HER2+ HR 1.49 are exploratory signals, not omission criteria; authors found **no subgroup for safe omission**.

studies.interpretation:
The central worry this cohort answers is whether better systemic therapy has absorbed the survival contribution of internal mammary node irradiation. The EBCTCG meta-analysis enrolled trials initiated before 2009, and DBCG IMN1 treated patients before taxanes and CT-based planning, so a skeptic could reasonably argue that the historical benefit belongs to an era of weaker drugs and cruder fields. DBCG IMN2 undercuts that argument directly: with taxane-based chemotherapy, aromatase inhibitors and trastuzumab, the OS hazard ratio of 0.85 is essentially the same point estimate as the EBCTCG rate ratio of 0.90 and the KROG 08-06 hazard ratio of 0.87. The Korean trial's null result reads better as an underpowered trial than as contrary evidence, and here the three estimates converge.

The design deserves careful weighting in both directions. Allocation by laterality is not randomization, but it is a close approximation: tumour side is unlikely to track prognosis, and the baseline table is balanced across nearly every variable. The residual concern is that laterality is not neutral for RT harm, since left-sided patients carry cardiac dose. That confounder works against the right-sided IMNI arm only if left-sided patients are healthier, which is implausible, and the heart-disease death rates (0.2% vs 0.7%) are small against an absolute OS difference of 4.2% at 15 years. The stronger methodological point runs the other way. Median IMN coverage in the left-sided controls was 20.4%, and 10.1% of them were deliberately treated, so the comparison is partial IMNI versus substantial incidental dose, not IMNI versus none. Dilution of this kind biases toward the null, which makes the observed effect a floor rather than a ceiling.

For the radiation oncologist, the decision this moves is the 1-3 node patient, where practice varies most. The HR of 0.85 (0.73-0.97) in that group is post hoc, and should be read as consistency with the overall result rather than an independent finding. It is still meaningful that the effect did not shrink as nodal burden fell, because the usual argument for omitting IMNI in N1 disease is that the absolute gain becomes too small to justify cardiac and lung dose. Here the 15-year cardiac death rates were low even with free-breathing wide tangents, and left-sided mean heart dose was 2.3 Gy.

Two subgroup signals invite overinterpretation. The medial/central, 4+ node HR of 0.98 inverts the long-held assumption that medial tumours benefit most, and the ER-/HER2+ HR of 1.49 suggests possible harm. Neither survives a multiplicity lens, the interaction test for location was non-significant, and NSABP B-51 did not show harm in HER2+ disease, albeit post-neoadjuvant. They are reasons to watch, not reasons to omit.

What this does not settle is the neoadjuvant population, which was excluded, and the IO and ADC era, whose effect on nodal RT benefit is unknown. It would be wrong if laterality carried an unmeasured prognostic imbalance of roughly the size of the effect, which the balanced baseline makes unlikely.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The 1-3 node HR 0.85 (0.73-0.97) addresses the group where IMN coverage is most contested, using 50 Gy/25 Fx free-breathing 3D tangents to ICS 1-4. Because incidental left-sided coverage (V90% 20.4%) dilutes the contrast, the benefit is likely understated with gated or VMAT coverage.

open_questions: Does IMNI benefit persist with adjuvant immunotherapy or ADCs?

sites.intro: For pelvic nodal oligorecurrence, elective pelvic RT beats MDT on MFS and locoregional RFS with no G2+ GU/GI toxicity difference. The benefit is concentrated in PSMA-staged pts with PSA <1.

studies.name: PEACE V-STORM
studies.tldr: 4yr MFS 76% vs 63% (HR 0.62, 80% CI 0.44-0.86) favoring whole-pelvis ENRT over MDT for pelvic nodal oligorecurrence, both with 6mo ADT.
details: 🔍 Phase 2 open-label RCT, 21 centres in 6 countries, N=196 randomised, 190 in mITT
📐 Two-sided α set at 0.20 with 80% CIs; p=0.063 clears that bar, not a conventional 0.05
🔍 ENRT: 45 Gy/25 fx whole pelvis (modified RTOG 2009, upper limit L4/L5) + SIB 65 Gy to PET+ nodes
🔍 MDT: SBRT 30 Gy/3 fx every other day (3 mm PTV margin) or sLND; sLND used in only 12 pts
💊 Both arms: 6 mo LHRH agonist/antagonist ADT

details.text: 📊 4yr outcomes, ENRT vs MDT (median f/u 50 mo)
📊 MFS subgroups (PET tracer prespecified; PSA and nodal level post hoc)

details: ⚠️ Prostate bed RT imbalance: 24 (25%) MDT vs 38 (41%) ENRT
⚠️ Post hoc: prostate bed in field → G2+ GI OR 4.6 (95% CI 1.5-15.8), p=0.0085
⚠️ No central PET review; ~1 in 5 staged with choline, not PSMA
🔗 vs GETUG-P07-OLIGOPELVIS (single-arm ENRT): 3yr bRFS 45% there, higher baseline PSA and choline staging

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase 2 hit its MFS primary at 50 mo median f/u, but was powered at α 0.20 with 80% CIs; authors call for phase 3 confirmation (POINTER-PC).
verdict.audience: Pelvic nodal oligorecurrence (≤5 PET+ nodes) after radical local prostate tx

studies.significance: The RT signal is regional: 4yr locoregional RFS 85% vs 62% (HR 0.45), consistent with MDT failing mostly in the pelvis. The benefit sat in PSMA-staged pts (HR 0.48) and PSA <1 (HR 0.27), so it moves the choice from nodal SBRT to whole-pelvis 45/25 with 65 Gy SIB. Prostate bed inclusion, not the pelvic field, drove added GI toxicity.
studies.monday_clinic: In a man with up to five PET-detected pelvic nodal recurrences below the aortic bifurcation after radical local treatment, this supports whole-pelvis ENRT with nodal SIB over nodal SBRT alone, both with 6 mo ADT; it does not extend to para-aortic, bone, or visceral disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Phase 2, open-label, randomised (1:1)** trial at 21 hospitals in Australia, Belgium, Italy, Norway, Spain, Switzerland. Minimisation stratified by **PET tracer** (choline vs PSMA) and **MDT type** (sLND vs SBRT/SIB). Median follow-up **50 mo** (IQR 42-58).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Biochemical relapse after RP, postoperative RT or definitive RT, with **≤5 PET-detected pelvic nodes** up to the aortic bifurcation. Excluded: bone/visceral mets, nodes above the bifurcation, **testosterone <50 ng/dL**. Median PSA 1.00 vs 0.85 ng/mL; 81% and 83% PSMA-staged.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **ENRT: 45 Gy/25 fx whole pelvis + 65 Gy SIB** to PET+ nodes, IMRT/VMAT mandatory. **MDT: SBRT 30 Gy/3 fx** every other day, 3 mm PTV margin, or extended sLND. Prostate bed RT ≥66 Gy/33 fx suggested for high-risk RP features in both arms, with benchmark-case QA.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **6 mo LHRH agonist or antagonist** in both arms, started no later than the first fraction. ADT was not to be restarted without clinical progression.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: MFS** (any M1 on PET or death). Secondary: bRFS, locoregional RFS, ADT-free survival, late G2+ GU/GI toxicity. OS, PCSS and time to castration resistance had too few events to report.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: 4yr cumulative G2+ GU **28% vs 31%** (p=0.73) and GI **7% vs 9%** (p=0.93), MDT vs ENRT. One ENRT pt had a recto-urethral fistula needing surgery. **No treatment-related deaths.**

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: First randomised comparison of MDT vs ENRT for nodal oligorecurrence. The single-arm GETUG-P07-OLIGOPELVIS reported **3yr bRFS 45%** with ENRT, in a higher-PSA, choline-staged cohort. POINTER-PC (phase 3) and GETUG-P12-OLIGOPELVIS 2 are the confirmatory tests.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents hormone-sensitive (testosterone ≥50 ng/dL) pts with ≤5 PET-positive pelvic nodes after radical local therapy, predominantly PSMA-staged. Does not represent para-aortic, bone or visceral recurrence, or pts on ongoing ADT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: **Prostate bed RT was unevenly used** (25% vs 41%) and linked to both local control and GI toxicity, which muddies attribution to the pelvic field. **No central PET review**, and the PSA and nodal-level subgroups are post hoc.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The MFS gain is mostly **prevention of further nodal (M1a) spread**, consistent with PSMA PET under-staging microscopic pelvic disease. It does not settle whether the benefit holds at higher PSA or with choline staging, or whether it reaches survival.

studies.interpretation:
The trial targets a question practice had already drifted into answering without randomised evidence. Nodal SBRT for PET-detected pelvic recurrence spread because it is short, targeted and tolerable, while whole-pelvis RT came with the intuition that anything visible on PET is the tip of a regional burden. PEACE V-STORM supports that intuition: the separation is carried by regional control, and the authors trace the MFS difference to prevented M1a nodal spread rather than to fewer bone or visceral events. That mechanism matters for how to read the result. ENRT is not buying systemic control; it is sterilising the pelvic nodal basin that PSMA PET cannot fully resolve, and MDT pts paid for that with repeat salvage (28 received another course of MDT).

The statistical frame deserves weight before the headline does. This is a screening phase 2 with α 0.20 and 80% CIs, and the primary p of 0.063 would not pass a conventional threshold. The direction is consistent across bRFS, locoregional RFS and ADT-free survival, which argues against chance, but the magnitude should be expected to shrink in a confirmatory trial. The authors themselves describe ENRT as a potential standard awaiting phase 3, and POINTER-PC is the trial that will decide it.

The subgroups point where the benefit likely lives. The effect was concentrated in PSMA-staged pts and those with PSA below 1, and absent with choline staging, PSA of 1 or higher, or common iliac involvement. Read together, ENRT seems to help most when disease is truly low-volume and pelvis-confined; once the burden is higher or already near the upper field edge, more lies outside the pelvis and a larger field adds little. Only the tracer split was prespecified, so these are hypothesis-generating, but they are biologically coherent and they narrow the population a reader should extrapolate to.

The prostate bed is the complication in this design. It was left to physician discretion, used more often in the ENRT arm, and in post hoc analysis tracked with both fewer local recurrences and more G2+ GI toxicity. Part of what looks like ENRT tolerability or ENRT benefit may therefore belong to prostate bed decisions rather than the pelvic nodal field. The encouraging finding is that the large pelvic field itself did not raise GI toxicity against SBRT, which weakens the main argument for the smaller field.

Against the ADT-sparing literature the authors cite (RADIOSA, EXTEND, EMBARK), the useful point is that local RT plus a short ADT course in both arms kept most pts off ADT for years. What remains unsettled is survival, which had too few events to report given near-universal cancer-specific survival in this setting, and whether the result survives central PET review and PSMA-only staging.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The RT signal is regional: 4yr locoregional RFS 85% vs 62% (HR 0.45), consistent with MDT failing mostly in the pelvis. The benefit sat in PSMA-staged pts (HR 0.48) and PSA <1 (HR 0.27), so it moves the choice from nodal SBRT to whole-pelvis 45/25 with 65 Gy SIB. Prostate bed inclusion, not the pelvic field, drove added GI toxicity.
